v2 KEEPS v1'S COST TEST -- THE BEST IDEA IN THIS FAMILY -- AND RETIRES ITS EMPTINESS CONCLUSION, WHICH IS FALSE AT HEAD AND WHOSE OWN REPRODUCTION COMMAND SAYS SO.

WHAT v1 CONCLUDED, VERBATIM: 'the net effect is that the lever's remaining population is EMPTY and the sweep lane built on it is closed'; FINDING 3: 'Adding the cost test -- keep a site only if a copy sourced from the folded register follows on our side and not the target's -- reduces L=9 to L-PAID=0. NOT ONE FUNCTION IN THE IMAGE currently pays a copy for an in-place fold that the target avoids'; DISPOSITION: 'init_player_change was the ONLY instance of the paid class in the image and it is already closed. ... there is no sweep to run today, and any future "extra address copy" residual should be screened with addrlo_inplace_census.py's L-PAID population rather than with P.'

WHAT ITS OWN TOOL PRINTS AT HEAD, measured for this record at e5eb50945, `python tools/gdl/addrlo_inplace_census.py` (exit 0): `L  ours IN_PLACE where target FRESH/VOL (LEVER) : 11` and `--- POPULATION L-PAID -- TRUE lever roster (in-place fold FORCES a copy) (n=1): game/enemy/critter ProcessCritterList gPlayers`, with the summary line `L=11 sites diverge in form; only 1 pay a copy for it -- the rest are cost-free @ha-temp choices.` The population is NOT empty, and its member is NOT the function v1's positive control names: v1's control was ui/select::init_player_change, which is closed and absent from L entirely at HEAD.

THE COST TEST ITSELF IS VINDICATED, NOT WEAKENED, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS SUPERSESSION. v1's mechanism -- an in-place fold is free unless it FORCES a copy, so screen with L-PAID and never with L or with P -- is confirmed by the very reading that kills its conclusion: L grew 9 -> 11 while L-PAID went 0 -> 1, so ten of eleven form-divergences remain cost-free exactly as v1 predicted. v1's FINDING 1 clause also holds unchanged: of the general-census P roster, exactly TWO members (combat::PlayerStartMissile, pmotion::PlayerMotion) appear in L at HEAD, as v1 states.

THE MERGED ANSWER NO SINGLE LIVE LAW STATED, and the reason this record and the AL v2 must be read together: the ONE row satisfying BOTH the V test (volatile destination, from `al_dest_split.py`) AND the L-PAID test (a copy is actually paid) is game/enemy/critter::ProcessCritterList -- and that row is measured INERT across three declaration orders, with a typed denial, in attempt.CR_processcritterlist-the-declaration-order-lever-is-inert-here-so-the-addr16lo-reachable-remainder-is-zero.20260904.v1. So the family's ACTIONABLE population is zero, but by an argument that needs both halves; v1 reached 'zero' by a route that is no longer true, and being right for a dead reason is what makes a law dangerous rather than merely stale. Screen with L-PAID, as v1 says; expect it non-empty; then check the row against its own attempt record before probing it.

A NEGATIVE CONTROL WORTH RECORDING, because it bears on a discrepancy flagged in the sibling supersession: v1's target-side instance counts REPRODUCE EXACTLY at HEAD. v1's FINDING 2 gives 'IN_PLACE/VOL target 976 ... FRESH/VOL target 1416 ... FRESH/CS target 920 ... IN_PLACE/CS is 0 on both sides'; HEAD prints `IN_PLACE/VOL 976`, `FRESH/VOL 1416`, `FRESH/CS 920`, `IN_PLACE/CS 0` on the TARGET column, with only the OURS column moving (962->966, 1489->1474, 887->891). That is the behaviour a retail-image-derived number MUST have across commits, and it is the control against which claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v2's unreconciled target-side shadow figure (2/33 published, 8/33 at HEAD) reads as anomalous. v1's inverse population moved with our side as expected: I=21 published, `I  target IN_PLACE where ours FRESH/VOL (inverse): 18` at HEAD.
